title: POC Weekly - incident playback & fallback design
summary: Short post-incident review of intermittent 5xx and timeout spikes during peak test window. Team walked through traces and hypothesis (thundering cache misses, burst at LB, retry storm). Redwood proposed a phased fallback and adaptive backoff plan: 1) rate-limit tuning + client-side jitter, 2) short-lived model variant fallback with degraded quality, 3) increased circuit-breaker thresholds and async queueing for non-blocking requests. Agreed next steps: share debug traces, run targeted load with KV cache priming, implement canary for fallback route, and follow up with SOC/kms notes for security team.
topics: Fallback model variants and quality tradeoffs
Security/audit log requirements for Private deployment
action_items: Laura Chen (Redwood AE): Share aggregated 5xx trace bundle + link to bench spreadsheet; due 2026-07-24
Mateo Rivera (SE): Provide config diff for circuit-breaker and suggested default backoff jitter; due 2026-07-24

transcript:
Header: 2026-07-22 15:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Attendees: Laura Chen, Mateo Rivera, Priya Nair (Redwood); Sanjay Patel, Maya Thompson, Oliver King, Eve Li (BrightAnchor)

[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick agenda — incident playback, root-cause notes, fallback design, and next steps. Maya, do you want to start with what you saw?

[00:28] Maya Thompson: Yeah thanks Laura. So during the 11:30 load window we saw a spike in 502/5xx, and a bunch of long tail timeouts. It looked like the ingress LB hit an unexpected burst of traffic. There was also a pattern where cold KV cache misses correlated to the spikes.

[01:12] Sanjay Patel: To add, the client side retry logic didn't have jitter, so we suspect a retry storm amplifying the backend load. We followed the logs, and a lot of calls clustered at the same 200ms boundary which is suspicious.

[01:47] Mateo Rivera: Interesting. On Redwood's side, the runtime emits per-request KV hit/miss and queue depth. In the traces you sent we see a short window where queue depth increases ~3x, then 50x latency on token generation and 5xx cascades.

[02:30] Oliver King: Can you explain the model fallback idea again? I remember from the doc there was a "degraded variant" concept but not the perf tradeoffs.

[03:05] Laura Chen: Sure. The idea is a short-lived model variant — lower-context or quantized — that is compatible but lower quality. When latency or error rate crosses threshold, traffic automatically routes to that variant for a bounded amount of time to keep the service available.

[03:48] Maya Thompson: That sounds useful, but we need strong guarantees around correctness for some routes. Some calls are customer-facing & sensitive.

[04:15] Eve Li: From security side, we also need audit logs for any fallback decisions — who triggered, what variant, and request metadata. Also KMS rotation and key usage must be logged.

[04:50] Mateo Rivera: Totally — Redwood can include an audit event in the trace for each fallback decision. We'll include the route, model id, timestamp, and a short reason code.

[05:22] Sanjay Patel: Back to root cause — can we walk the timeline? Maya, you said cold KV misses. Does that mean the cache eviction/TTL interplay with bursty test traffic?

[06:01] Maya Thompson: Yeah TTLs were default. We had a big churn and priming didn't happen because the load pattern was new. The first 10–15 minutes had lower hit rate. Once primed, latencies improved. So cache cold start plus simultaneous retries likely pushed queues over.

[06:40] Laura Chen: That suggests two actionable levers: client-side backoff/jitter to prevent retry storms, and server-side short-term admission control (circuit-breaker) to shed or queue overload gracefully.

[07:25] Mateo Rivera: For circuit-breakers we usually recommend a sliding window error threshold with exponential backoff and jitter. Also add a short queue with async response for non-blocking requests where possible.

[08:04] Oliver King: On the data plane, if we route to a quantized model variant, do we need to change client code? Or is it routing-layer only?

[08:32] Laura Chen: Routing-layer only. The API call stays the same; the control plane switches the model id. We recommend tagging the response so clients can optionally log quality metrics on their side.

[09:10] Maya Thompson: Let's talk numbers — what thresholds should we set for canary? We don't want too agressive fallback triggering.

[09:40] Mateo Rivera: A pragmatic approach: set initial threshold at 3% 5xx per 1-minute sliding window or p95 latency above 1.2x of baseline for two consecutive windows. Canary window 30 minutes, observe error delta and user-facing metric impact.

[10:15] Sanjay Patel: Sounds fine. Also it's important to have an immediate rollback if we see quality regressions. How do we measure quality automatically?

[10:40] Laura Chen: Redwood can instrument a small set of golden prompts for the fallback path and produce a similarity score versus baseline. If score drops below a configurable threshold, we auto-revert.

[11:18] Eve Li: For SOC 2 evidence, can you include a note of the audit log schema and the retention period? We need to map to our internal controls.

[11:42] Priya Nair: We'll attach the audit log schema and a doc on retention policies. Default retention in hosted is 90 days; for Private you can configure longer with your own storage.

[12:05] Maya Thompson: Regarding retries — we will add jitter client-side, but we also want a server-side limit to capped retries per IP/ token.

[12:32] Mateo Rivera: We can recommend rate-limit buckets per token and an adaptive token-based leaky bucket. Also instrument a request hash so you can detect replays.

[13:05] Sanjay Patel: A couple of anomalies in the traces: some requests that timed out upstream still returned partial token stream; transcription from some events looked garbled. Could be a streaming edge-case.

[13:40] Laura Chen: Yep streaming can expose partials if the backend container dies during generation. We'll add improved truncation semantics and a marker that flags partial responses.

[14:12] Maya Thompson: For our POC success criteria, we care about error rate under 0.5% at p95 latency < 600ms for normalized requests during peak. If we can't meet that we need a degradation plan with fallback.

[14:45] Mateo Rivera: We'll aim to meet that with a combination of priming, retry jitter, and fallback policy.

[15:10] Oliver King: Can Redwood share the config diff you mentioned for circuit-breaker? We prefer to review before applying.

[15:30] Mateo Rivera: Yes I'll export a sample config and include recommended tuning values.

[16:05] Sanjay Patel: About priming — what does priming look like operationally? Is this automated or manual?

[16:30] Laura Chen: It can be both. You can trigger a priming job that walks a representative prompt set and warms the KV cache and kernel paths. For production, we recommend scheduled low-cost priming during predictable windows.

[17:05] Maya Thompson: We'll try a priming run before the next heavy test and report results.

[17:30] Eve Li: Also, regarding KMS — what's the rotation window and support for HSM? We need to map to our key policy.

[17:55] Priya Nair: Redwood supports external KMS/HSM integrations in Private deployments. We'll send the HSM integration guide and the KMS rotation options (30/90/365 days).

[18:22] Laura Chen: Quick note — competitors were mentioned by the team earlier (MegaCloud AI and OpenServ). We discussed differences around built-in fallback and audit trace clarity.

[18:50] Oliver King: Anything else?

[19:00] Sanjay Patel: One more thing — can we capture an example of a failed request and replay it locally? The traces you share should include a request id and full headers.

[19:22] Mateo Rivera: We'll ensure the traces include id, timestamps, route, and KV hit/miss annotations.

[19:45] Laura Chen: Great. Action items recap — share traces, config diffs, and SOC docs. Can we aim to reconvene in four days to review the priming run?

[20:05] Oliver King: Yes four days works.

[20:20] Maya Thompson: I'll run the priming job tomorrow and aim to have initial numbers by Tuesday.

[20:40] Laura Chen: Perfect. We'll also prepare the canary runbook and rollback plan. Thanks everyone.

[21:00] (meeting winds down, some folks drop)

[45:00] -- End of recording (remaining time was Q&A and scheduling which were clipped in the export)

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had some mis-attributed speaker tags and a few garbled product names (e.g., "kv cache" transcribed as "kay-vee cache", "fallback" sometimes appears as "fall back"), typical for Fireflies exports.
